Yes, writing the note there feels natural — it's a roomy spot right in the bookmark's details, and the little prompt about why I'm saving it nudges me in the right way. Jotting "Use this for the museum renovation ideas" felt like leaving myself a sticky note on the link.

And the balance is right. I wouldn't want my notes crowding up the library cards — those should stay clean and glanceable — so tucking the note inside the details is the right home for it. The important part is that you've said the words in my note still get searched, because that's often how I'd actually find something again ("that link I saved about renovation ideas"). Good.

Two things I'd want to confirm when we get to it: that when I come back and open a bookmark later, I can actually read the note I left, and that if I put a little formatting in it — a couple of bullet points, say — it shows up nicely rather than as raw symbols. Can we check that at some point?
